audit_question.question: Can takeSnapshot consume a nil FileSnapshotSink.Close return as permission to record snapshot metadata and compact logs when an earlier terminal call on that same sink did not publish a usable snapshot, or do the sink contract and caller control flow exclude that interpretation?
audit_question.importance: If snapshot completion permits reclamation without usable replacement recovery evidence, restart or replica recovery could lose required history. This is a potential consequence; neither the triggering history nor actual data loss has been established.
contexts: Built-in file snapshot store when selected
Sequential terminal calls on the same sink
event_paths: takeSnapshot -> FSMSnapshot.Persist -> sink terminal call -> takeSnapshot Close -> snapshot metadata update and compaction
counterevidence: The inventory describes takeSnapshot as requiring both Persist and Close to return nil before proceeding; propagation of an earlier terminal error may exclude the suspected path.

The inventory distinguishes full first-close publication from the already-closed return. Correct terminal-call ownership or an applicable Persist contract may make that distinction harmless to this consumer.
The inventory lists metadata writing, rename and parent synchronization on the first-close publication path; their exact guards and error handling require source review.
unknowns: The applicable SnapshotSink and FSMSnapshot.Persist contracts, including terminal-call ownership and error propagation.
Whether a permitted Persist execution can return nil after an unsuccessful or cancelling terminal call.
Whether repeated Close returns preserve an earlier failure or merely observe the terminal latch.
The precise relationship between accepted Close, snapshot metadata updates and log compaction.
Whether any candidate local contract applies independently of unspecified application behavior.
The actual selected snapshot-store and filesystem configuration.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The inventory identifies a concrete representation difference: a terminal latch suppresses subsequent work, whereas successful publication requires several fallible operations. It also identifies a consumer that proceeds after a nil Close return. Exact source must establish whether these paths can interact under the applicable interface contract.

selection_rationale: Select consumption of F_snapshot_close_accepted because the inventory supplies both a specific terminal-result ambiguity and its reclamation consumer. Reading the contracts and control flow can distinguish excluded misuse or reliable error propagation from an attributable local completion relation. An excluded path would explain this hypothesis; an applicable ambiguous success path would support a bounded check, while unspecified application obligations could leave applicability unresolved. F_recorded_match consumption is another consequential option, but its remote producer and commit consumer remain unread and require more initial reconstruction. F_batch_callback_returned offers a single-versus-batch comparison, but the current inventory identifies no comparable consumer mismatch. No attached implementation source currently supports an obligation or terminal disposition.

reading_requests.reason: Acquire snapshot interfaces and the complete takeSnapshot and compaction control flow to establish terminal-call semantics, error propagation and the exact reclamation consumer.
Acquire the FSM snapshot persistence contract, especially sink ownership and required handling of Close or Cancel outcomes.
Inspect Close and Cancel declarations and terminal branches, including the closed latch, publication steps, returned errors and repeated-call results.
